question.text: Will the IOM Missing Migrants Project record at least 2,500 Mediterranean migrant deaths in 2026?
question.resolution_criteria: This question resolves as **Yes** if the IOM Missing Migrants Project incident dataset shows that the year-to-date sum of dead plus missing for calendar 2026 for “Mediterranean” is at least 2,500.The primary source is the IOM Missing Migrants Project public site : https://missingmigrants.iom.int/region/mediterranean
question.fine_print: In case of reporting delays, resolution may be delayed until January 10, 2027. If still unresolved at that date, the question may resolve as **No** based on the information available at the time, regardless of reporting delays. Subsequent additions or revisions will not cause the question to reresolve.

research:
As of the latest data on 2026-11-03, the IOM page shows 2,045 dead and missing in the Mediterranean for 2026, so another 455 must be recorded by resolution. I'm summarizing the findings now. I found no market or expert forecast on this question.

## 1. Resolution source
- 2026-11-03 (checked): The IOM Missing Migrants Project data page shows **2,045 dead and missing in the Mediterranean for 2026**. The page says the latest recorded incident is dated **23 October 2026**. [IOM data](https://missingmigrants.iom.int/data)
- Earlier full years on the same page: 2025: 2,185; 2024: 2,573; 2023: 3,155; 2022: 2,411; 2021: 2,048; 2020: 1,450; 2019: 1,885; 2018: 2,337; 2017: 3,139. [IOM data](https://missingmigrants.iom.int/data)
- The region page named in the question shows only the cumulative figure since 2014 (35,705). Its extracted incident list seemed to stop at Dec 2025, but its disclaimer also gives the 23 Oct 2026 latest incident. [IOM Mediterranean](https://missingmigrants.iom.int/region/mediterranean)

## 2. Current status
- Nothing has settled the question yet. Reaching 2,500 needs about **455 more** recorded between 23 Oct and the resolution snapshot (by 10 Jan 2027 at the latest). That is roughly 2.3 months of incidents plus any late-entered records.
- 2026 is running below 2025's final total (2,185) but is still about 10 weeks from year-end.

## 3. Recent news (newest first)
- 2026-11-02: Alarm Phone reported a missing boat carrying 10 people. It left Boumerdès, Algeria, on 26 Oct (Western Med). If IOM confirms it, this adds about 10. [Europa Press](https://www.europapress.es/illes-balears/noticia-alertan-desaparicion-patera-diez-personas-bordo-salio-argelia-26-octubre-20261102202549.html)
- 2026-11-02: At least 7 died on a boat near Lanzarote. This is the **Atlantic route, which does not count** toward the Mediterranean total. [Observador](https://observador.pt/2026/11/02/pelo-menos-sete-migrantes-mortos-em-barco-com-140-pessoas-a-caminho-de-canarias/)
- ~2026-09-29 to 10-04 (sources disagree on the date): A wreck off Tunisia left 2 dead and at least 6 missing (Sea-Watch). [MarineLink](https://www.marinelink.com/news/two-dead-six-missing-migrant-shipwreck-543343)
- 2026-10-09: The Djibouti wreck (139 dead, 84 missing) is **outside the Mediterranean**. [Al Jazeera](https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2026/10/11/at-least-109-dead-over-100-missing-as-migrant-boat-capsizes-off-djibouti)
- 2026-09-18: IOM counted 2,292 dead or missing in 2026 across the Mediterranean and Atlantic, against 1,999 for the same period of 2025. That breaks down as Central Med 996, Eastern Med 417, and Spain routes (Atlantic plus Western Med) 879. [Manorama](https://www.manoramayearbook.in/current-affairs/world/2026/09/18/migrant-fatalities-along-central-mediterranean-route-rise.html)
- 2026-04-07: IOM reported about 990 Mediterranean deaths, calling it one of the deadliest starts since 2014. [IOM](https://www.iom.int/news/over-180-feared-dead-mediterranean-death-toll-nears-1000-2026)
- 2026-02: IOM reported at least 606 by early February, the deadliest start since 2014. Cyclone Harry in January accounted for about 430 Central Med deaths. [Daily Sabah](https://www.dailysabah.com/world/europe/at-least-606-migrants-dead-or-missing-in-mediterranean-so-far-in-2026)

## 4. Base rates
- Of the last 9 full years (2017-2025), the Mediterranean reached 2,500 or more in 3: 2017, 2023 and 2024.
- 2026's pace has slowed a lot. The count went from about 990 in early April to 2,045 by 23 Oct, about 160 a month. At that rate, 23 Oct to 31 Dec adds roughly 360, giving about 2,400 or more.
- Late-year growth in 2025 suggests a lot of additions in the final weeks or after the fact:
  - In mid-Nov 2025, IOM put Central Med deaths just over 1,000 for the year. [Ada Derana](https://www.adaderana.lk/news.php?nid=114635)
  - Reuters in Jan 2026 cited 1,340 for the Central Med. [search summary](https://www.internazionale.it/ultime-notizie-reuters/2026/01/26/hundreds-feared-missing-or-dead-trying-to-cross-the-mediterranean-says-un-migration-agency)
  - The Mediterranean full-year figure was 2,185. [Libya Security Monitor](https://libyasecuritymonitor.com/deaths-of-migrants-at-sea-remain-high/)
  - A Nov 2025 figure of about 1,500 for the whole Mediterranean, attributed to the BBC, comes from a secondary search snippet I could not verify.
- Single big wrecks (50 to 600 deaths) can swing the outcome on their own. Winter weather tends to reduce crossings but raise how lethal each one is.

## 5. Other forecasts
- I found no Polymarket, Kalshi, Manifold or Metaculus market on Mediterranean migrant deaths. The Kalshi and Polymarket prices supplied (remittances, Hormuz traffic, Supreme Court, sports betting law) are **not relevant**.

## 6. Upcoming events before resolution
- Nov-Dec 2026 crossings, especially Libya and Tunisia to Italy, the Crete route, and Algeria to Spain or the Balearics. One mass-casualty wreck could close most of the 455 gap.
- IOM catch-up entries: the data lags (latest incident 23 Oct as of 3 Nov). Bodies washing up in Libya and "invisible shipwrecks" are often added in batches.
- The question resolves from IOM data around 1 Jan 2027, with a possible delay to 10 Jan 2027. IOM's annual release, usually in Jan-Feb, may come after the resolution snapshot.

Sources: [IOM data](https://missingmigrants.iom.int/data), [IOM Mediterranean](https://missingmigrants.iom.int/region/mediterranean), [IOM April release](https://www.iom.int/news/over-180-feared-dead-mediterranean-death-toll-nears-1000-2026), [Manorama](https://www.manoramayearbook.in/current-affairs/world/2026/09/18/migrant-fatalities-along-central-mediterranean-route-rise.html), [Daily Sabah](https://www.dailysabah.com/world/europe/at-least-606-migrants-dead-or-missing-in-mediterranean-so-far-in-2026), [Al Jazeera April](https://aljazeera.com/news/2026/4/7/mediterranean-migrant-deaths-mounting-towards-1000-in-2026-un), [MarineLink](https://www.marinelink.com/news/two-dead-six-missing-migrant-shipwreck-543343), [Europa Press](https://www.europapress.es/illes-balears/noticia-alertan-desaparicion-patera-diez-personas-bordo-salio-argelia-26-octubre-20261102202549.html), [Observador](https://observador.pt/2026/11/02/pelo-menos-sete-migrantes-mortos-em-barco-com-140-pessoas-a-caminho-de-canarias/), [Ada Derana](https://www.adaderana.lk/news.php?nid=114635), [Libya Security Monitor](https://libyasecuritymonitor.com/deaths-of-migrants-at-sea-remain-high/), [Al Jazeera Djibouti](https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2026/10/11/at-least-109-dead-over-100-missing-as-migrant-boat-capsizes-off-djibouti), [Internazionale/Reuters](https://www.internazionale.it/ultime-notizie-reuters/2026/01/26/hundreds-feared-missing-or-dead-trying-to-cross-the-mediterranean-says-un-migration-agency)

That leaves **455** to reach 2,500 by 31 December, about 45 a week over roughly 10 weeks.

### 1. Resolution source

- 2026-11-03 (fetched): the Mediterranean region page has the same "latest incident 23 October 2026" note. My page reader couldn't extract a 2026 figure from its charts. It did show the cumulative figure since 2014: 35,705. [MMP Mediterranean](https://missingmigrants.iom.int/region/mediterranean)

### 2. Current status

### 3. Recent news (newest first)
- 2026-11-02: Alarm Phone (a migrant hotline group) reported that a boat with **10 people**, which left Boumerdès, Algeria on 26 Oct, has disappeared. That is the Western Mediterranean, so it would count if IOM records it. - 2026-09-17: IOM figures through 15 Sep: Central Mediterranean **996** (844 in the same period of 2025), Eastern Mediterranean **417** (284), Spain including the Atlantic **879**. Arrivals to Europe fell 39%. [IOM](https://www.iom.int/news/new-iom-data-migrant-arrivals-europe-fall-39-2026-while-deaths-continue-rise)
- 2026-04-07: IOM said 990 dead and missing so far in 2026. [IOM](https://www.iom.int/news/over-180-feared-dead-mediterranean-death-toll-nears-1000-2026)
- 2026-02-23: 606 so far in 2026, "the deadliest start to a year" since 2014, largely because of Cyclone Harry in January. [IOM](https://www.iom.int/news/30-migrants-dead-or-missing-greece-latest-tragedy-mediterranean)

### 4. Base rates
- **Pace in 2026:**
  - 1 Jan to 23 Feb: 606, about 79 a week.
  - 23 Feb to 7 Apr: 384, about 63 a week.
  - 7 Apr to 23 Oct: 1,055, about **37 a week**.
  - Hitting 2,500 needs about 45 a week from 23 Oct, which is above the pace since April.
- **Past full-year Mediterranean totals:**
  - 2025: **2,185**, from a UN/IOM media asset, with other reports saying at least 2,108. [UN media](https://media.un.org/avlibrary/en/asset/d353/d3539494)
  - 2024: one search summary said 3,041. I could not verify that, and I recall the MMP figure as about 2,450.
- **Late-year additions:** an Italian article from about 25 Nov 2025 said "nearly 1,700" died at sea trying to reach Europe in 2025, and the final 2025 figure was 2,185. If both numbers are Mediterranean MMP counts, the total grew by about 400 or more after late November, through new incidents plus backfilled records. I could not confirm the region or date of the 1,700 figure. [L'Indipendente](https://www.lindipendente.online/2025/11/25/nel-2025-quasi-1-700-esseri-umani-sono-morti-in-mare-per-raggiungere-leuropa/?pdf=166881)
- **Big wrecks:** one large Libyan or Greek shipwreck with 100 or more dead or missing can cover a large share of the gap. Wrecks of that size have happened in several recent years.

### 5. Other forecasts
- None of the supplied Kalshi or Polymarket markets (remittances, Hormuz traffic, Supreme Court cases and others) matches this question.
- I found no prediction market or expert forecast on Mediterranean migrant deaths in 2026.

### 6. Upcoming events before resolution
- Winter storms in November and December, especially on the Central Mediterranean (Libya and Tunisia) and around Crete and the Aegean. The January 2026 cyclone alone produced about 430 deaths.
- IOM may backfill late-October and November incidents, including the Algerian boat with 10 people.
- IOM periodic releases, and its usual year-end or early-January statement. Resolution can wait for data until 10 January 2027, but later revisions will not change the outcome.
- Watch the MMP homepage figure and its "latest incident" date for updates.

forecasts.reasoning:
(a) About 2 months remain. Resolution is based on the IOM snapshot around 1 January 2027, with a possible delay to 10 January 2027. For Yes, IOM's Mediterranean dead plus missing total for 2026 must reach at least 2,500. That requires about 455 more recorded on top of the 2,045 shown as of 3 November, where the latest recorded incident is dated 23 October. The additions can come from new incidents between 23 October and 31 December, or from late entries for earlier incidents.

(b) If nothing changed, the total stays at 2,045 and the question resolves No. With normal accrual, the projected total is around 2,400, which is still short of the threshold.

(c) Base rate: in 3 of the last 9 full years (2017-2025), the Mediterranean total reached 2,500 or more, about 33%. The better reference class is "a year sitting near 2,045 by late October." The threshold is reached only when late-year accrual exceeds about 450, which happens in a minority of years, perhaps 25-40%.

(d) Evidence for Yes:
- 2026 started very deadly, with about 990 deaths by 7 April.
- On 18 September, IOM said the combined Mediterranean and Atlantic toll was running above the 2025 pace.
- Late-year additions in 2025 looked large. Central Med went from about 1,000 in mid-November 2025 to about 1,340 cited in January.
- Single mass-casualty wrecks of 100 or more are common. Data lag also means some late-October and November incidents are not yet entered.

Evidence for No:
- The pace slowed to about 160 a month from April to October. That projects only about 360 more by year-end, giving roughly 2,400.
- Recent news (2 November) shows only small Mediterranean incidents, around 10 at a time.
- Winter weather reduces the number of crossings.
- The early-January snapshot may miss December entries that IOM adds later.

(e) No scenario: November and December bring the usual scattered small wrecks off Libya, Tunisia and Algeria, adding about 300-400. With lag, the total is around 2,350-2,450 on 10 January.

Yes scenario: a single large shipwreck off Libya or near Crete with 150-300 missing, together with batch entries of bodies recovered in Libya, pushes the total past 2,500 in December.

(f) I start at the roughly 33% base rate. The trend projection falls just under the threshold, so the outcome depends on whether a large wreck occurs or catch-up entries are big. Those are plausible but not the most likely case, and the timing of the snapshot works against Yes. Late-year growth patterns in 2025 partly offset this. On balance I stay near the base rate, slightly below it.

Probability: 32%

(a) The outcome should be known around 1 to 10 January 2027, about 9 to 10 weeks from now. For Yes, the IOM Missing Migrants Project must show at least 2,500 dead plus missing in the Mediterranean for calendar 2026. As of 3 November it shows 2,045, with the latest incident dated 23 October. So about 455 more must be recorded, covering late October to December incidents plus any backfilled entries, before the snapshot.

(b) If nothing changed, the count stays at 2,045 and the question resolves No. Realistically the count will keep rising. At the April to October pace of about 160 per month, it lands near 2,400 to 2,420, which is still short of 2,500.

(c) Base rate: 3 of the last 9 full years (2017 to 2025) reached 2,500, about 33%. The better reference class is the chance of adding about 455 or more between late October and early January. Nov-Dec Mediterranean totals usually run roughly 250 to 450. Larger late-year jumps have happened in some years, often through backfilled records and big wrecks. Conditional on this starting point, my base rate is about 30 to 40%.

(d) Evidence for Yes:
- 2026 had the deadliest start on record: 606 by early February and about 990 by 7 April.
- On 18 September, IOM said the combined Mediterranean and Atlantic toll was running above 2025's.
- In 2025 the Central Mediterranean count grew a lot late: just over 1,000 in mid-November, then 1,340 cited in January 2026. This points to big backfills.

- One mass-casualty wreck of 100 or more would close much of the gap.

Evidence for No:
- The pace has slowed sharply since spring, to about 160 per month.
- 2026 is currently behind 2025's final total of 2,185.
- Winter tends to reduce the number of crossings.
- Incidents in late December may not be entered by the 1 to 10 January snapshot.
- The Atlantic deaths near Lanzarote and the Djibouti wreck do not count.

(e) No scenario: November and December bring scattered small incidents, adding about 300 to 400 in total. IOM's backfill largely arrives after mid-January, and the snapshot reads about 2,380 to 2,450.

Yes scenario: A large Libya-to-Italy or Crete-route shipwreck with 100 or more missing, plus routine incidents and a batch of bodies recovered in Libya entered in December, pushes the total past 2,500 by early January.

(f) No relevant market exists. I start at about 35% from the conditional base rate. The extrapolated trend sits about 80 to 100 short of the threshold, which pulls the estimate down. The variance is high, though: big wrecks are common, and IOM's late-year backfilling in 2025 was large, which pulls it back up. I end slightly above the trend-only estimate.

Probability: 38%

**(a) Time left and what Yes requires.** About 8 to 9 weeks remain. The question resolves from the IOM data page around 1 January 2027, with a possible delay to 10 January 2027. For Yes, the 2026 Mediterranean dead-plus-missing count must rise from 2,045 (latest incident 23 October) to at least 2,500. That means about 455 more records must be added by the snapshot. They can come from new incidents or from late entries for past ones.

**(b) Status quo.** If nothing more were recorded, the total would stay at 2,045 and the question resolves No. Some additions are certain, so the real question is whether they reach 455.

**(c) Base rate.** In 3 of the 9 full years from 2017 to 2025, the Mediterranean total reached 2,500, about 33%. The better reference class is conditional on 2026's pace. Adding 455 or more in roughly the last 10 weeks plus backfill is unusual. It requires about 200 a month, above 2026's recent average of about 160 a month. Conditional base rate: about 30 to 40%.

**(d) Strongest evidence.**
- **For Yes:**
  - 2025 showed large late-year growth. Central Med was just over 1,000 in mid-November 2025 and 1,340 by January 2026.
  - IOM entries lag, as of 3 November the latest incident was 23 October, so October records are probably still incomplete.
  - The count apparently jumped quickly between mid-September and 23 October.
  - One 100 to 300 death wreck off Libya, Tunisia or Crete could close most of the gap.
  - Winter crossings are more lethal per trip.
- **For No:**
  - Since April the pace has been about 160 a month (990 on 7 April to 2,045 on 23 October). That projects to only about 2,400 by year-end.
  - Crossings fall in November and December.
  - The snapshot near 1 January will miss late-December incidents that have not yet been entered.
  - The 2025 final of 2,185 includes backfill added through most of 2026, which this question's snapshot will not get.

**(e) Scenarios.**
- **No:** November and December bring a steady trickle of small wrecks in the Central and Western Med (10 to 40 deaths each), with no single mass-casualty event. The page shows about 2,350 to 2,450 on 1 to 10 January.
- **Yes:** A large wreck off Libya or near Crete in November or December (more than 150 dead or missing), plus IOM backfill of bodies recovered in Libya, pushes the count past 2,500 by early January.

**(f) From base rate to final probability.** I start at about 33% from the unconditional base rate. Linear extrapolation puts the expected total slightly below the threshold, roughly 2,400 to 2,450. The distribution has a heavy right tail because of mass-casualty events and backfill, and the 2025 pattern of late surges pulls the estimate up somewhat. Snapshot timing and the winter drop in crossings pull it down. Net, I stay close to the base rate.
